title: Tourist Attractions
text: It was when we loaded the carriage full of provisions and headed toward the eastern part of the country.
“This village sure is bustling.”

We passed through a village teeming with adventurers. There’s a mountain range nearby, isn’t there? Taking a break from selling provisions, I put on my robe and headed toward the village tavern with my Father.
“It seems to be thriving.”
Since he’s been the topic of conversation among the Saints of the Divine Bird, the villagers seem to know who my Father is.
“Yes, about a week ago, the Sword Hero defeated a vicious dragon living in the mountains. Now, adventurers are gathering here to procure materials for weapons and armor from that dragon.”
“Huh…”
Hmm… the dragon that Ren defeated, you say? It seems Ren has been subtly making his way toward Zeltoble since taking on this job.
“What do you think? Should we go check it out too?”
“Is that really necessary?”
My Father asks me. I don’t really have any idea what’s going on around here.
“There are even people searching for the treasure the dragon left behind now. Come on, haven’t you seen the guild bulletin board?”
“W-well, I did check it out. But we’re just traveling merchants.”
“Thanks to the Holy Ones of the Divine Bird, the village looks set to become even more prosperous.”
“Hahaha.”
The conversation between Father and the tavern owner comes to a subtle close. After having a light meal at the tavern, Father looks toward the mountains.
“I’ve got some dragon-related materials stashed away in my shield, but…”
“Are you worried about it?”
“Well, yeah.”
“I really don’t like dragons.”
“Yeah, I know. Sakura-chan and the others overreact to dragons, too.”

Filolial-sama and dragons are sworn enemies. Any dragon that opposes Filolial-sama and his kind is practically my enemy as well. That’s why I couldn’t really care less about all the commotion in this village.
“Treasure left behind by a dragon, huh…”

Just then, some adventurers—who appeared to have just come down from the mountain—were discussing something with their companions, their eyes gleaming. After listening to the conversation, the adventurers headed back up the mountain.
“Isn’t it a bit too intense for just gathering materials? Even if it’s lively…”
“Isn’t an area with a dragon’s carcass a bit too tough for ordinary adventurers?”
“Ah, there’s a level cap, after all. Or maybe the monsters are surprisingly strong… Still, there sure are a lot of adventurers bringing back monster carcasses.”
“That’s true.”

From what I can see, there are all kinds of monsters here. While there’s a wide variety, I get the impression there aren’t many dragon-type ones. However, there are some monsters that look like a hybrid between a dragon and another species.
“I wonder what kind of creatures dragons are in this world?”
“I haven’t the faintest idea.”

They say it’s good to know your enemy, but to me, dragons are nothing more than monsters that provide excellent EXP and loot. Come to think of it, there were a few people in Father’s village who knew a lot about monsters. I should ask them, but I don’t know where they are.
“I had the impression that dragon territories—besides the alpha dragon—were full of dragon-type monsters, but it seems I was wrong.”
“Now that you mention it, you’re right.”

But isn’t that to be expected? However, even from a distance, the monster carcasses the adventurers are carrying don’t seem to be limited to dragon-type monsters. If anything, I get the feeling there are more of other kinds. Father seems concerned about this. What could this mean?
“The dragon Ren defeated… I wonder what kind of dragon it was? Was it a boss-class dragon or something?”
“It’s not impossible.”
“I’ve helped take down one before too… it was a pretty huge dragon. Do you think that dragon’s just been left out in the mountains?”
“Judging by the crowd of adventurers gathering there, I’d say it’s probably in the mountains, wouldn’t you?”
“Maybe. The creatures mixed in with the dragons being brought here are all small, and it looks like some adventurers are even proudly showing off large scales from time to time.”
And so, Father is looking toward the mountains with a worried expression.
“Is something worrying you?”

“Yeah. Even if they call it ‘materials,’ leaving a dragon’s carcass out there could cause all sorts of problems, don’t you think? The meat and organs will rot… I just hope it doesn’t lead to an epidemic or something.”
“An epidemic, you say… Do diseases that come from dragon carcasses actually kill people?”
Unfortunately, I don’t know much about dragons. To be honest, I have absolutely no interest in them at all.

“Yeah. I don’t know about this world, but in fantasy, there are actually quite a few stories about how to deal with dragon corpses. In those stories, it seems to involve HP or Magical Power, but I wonder how it really works in reality.”
“Either way, since they’re living creatures, wouldn’t they just rot?”

“Well, if you think about it normally, that’s true. …Rot?　It’s kind of scary to think they might turn into dragon zombies. They’re a classic monster in RPGs, and sometimes they’re even stronger than when they were alive.”
“There were dragon zombies in *Emerald Online*, the game I used to play, too.”

My father fell deep in thought at my words. In the game, dragon corpses didn’t turn into dragon zombies—instead, there were dungeons where dragon zombies appeared. They were basically mid-game enemies.
“Um… if I remember correctly from what Motoyasu-kun said, a lot of that game knowledge is actually wrong. But I still feel like dragon zombies are the kind of thing that could actually exist.”
“Well then, shall we go and put our minds at ease first?”
“…Yeah, you’re right. It doesn’t seem like it’ll be very profitable, but if using dragon-based weapons and armor will actually make a difference in this country, then maybe it’s worth it.”
My father agreed and headed over to Keel and the others, who were out peddling their wares.
“Hey, guys, what’s up?”
“Well, apparently there’s a dragon that was defeated on that mountain, so we thought we’d go get some materials.”
“Oh, really! Should we go too, then?”
Sakura and the others are getting ready to go. They’d been looking bored, after all. They’re probably happy to get some exercise.
“It’d be a disaster if someone stole the food we’re carrying, so I’d like someone to keep watch. Anyone want to stay behind…?”
“Oink!”
The Lazy Pig took this as a golden opportunity and oinked. He’s raising his hand as if to say, “I’ll go first!”
“Elena-san and…”
“So that means I get to go!”

Keel is cheerfully raising his arms in celebration. Father turns his gaze toward Filolial-sama and the others. Sakura-chan looks like she wants to go with Father. Yuki-chan and Kou also seem to want to come along—probably because they’re bored. Luna-chan is riding on Keel’s back.
“Hmm… Let’s draw lots to see who stays behind.”
Filolial-sama and the others quickly drew the lots that Father had prepared. I sensed a faint hint of hostility. As a result, Yuki-chan and Kou were chosen to stay behind.
“That’s too bad.”
“Too bad… Can I eat some of the food that’s piled up here?”
“Just a little bit, then.”
Father gave Kou, who was staying behind, permission. Kou is delighted.
“Yay!”
“Yuki-chan, I’m counting on you to keep watch.”
“I’m really motivated now!”
Yuki-chan is very responsible, which is a huge help. She also loves to run. Once Father and I return from the mountain, let’s take Yuki-chan and the others there again.
“Well then, let’s get going!”
“Ooh!”
Riding on Sakura-chan and Luna-chan, who had transformed into their Filolial forms, we headed toward the mountains.
“Hmm… how should I put it? It’s turned into a tourist spot, hasn’t it…”

My Father said in a tone that suggested he was a bit dumbfounded. The path had been paved like a hiking trail all the way up to the middle of the mountain, and men who appeared to be villagers were keeping an eye on the adventurers. We kept moving along that path, and it’s true… it definitely has the atmosphere of a tourist spot you’d visit on a school trip. We even had to pay an entrance fee just to enter the mountain, so it’s practically no different from a tourist attraction.
“But the maintenance is half-baked, isn’t it?”

My father muttered as he surveyed the mountain scenery. Sure, there are paved roads and such, but they all look like they were thrown together in a hurry. Well, it’s been only a little over a week since Ren defeated the dragon, so I suppose this is to be expected.
“You’re right.”

Every now and then, creatures—some of which look like dragons—attack us almost by surprise. The adventurers seemed to be fighting those monsters while screaming and yelping. As for us? Since fighting might give away our true identities, we left it to Sakura, Luna, and Keel.
“You know, in about a hundred years, I bet a church will be built here, calling it ‘the legendary site where the Sword Hero fought a deadly battle against a dragon.’”
“Admission will be one silver coin, I suppose.”
“Ahaha…”
My Father let out a dry laugh. It’s certainly rare to see a dragon’s territory developed this much, but I wonder about this whole “you need money for everything” thing?
